title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this page and its neighbours. We work in an abelian k-linear category C_0 with a sequence of objects Psi^i satisfying:
- End(Psi^i) = k;
- Hom(Psi^i, Psi^j) = 0 for i != j;
- Ext^1(Psi^i, Psi^{i-1}) is one-dimensional with basis e_i (hypothesis (C) on the previous page).

Phi^i is the extension of Psi^i by Psi^{i-1} with class e_i. Phi(i,n) (written L(i,n) in the neighbouring transcriptions) is the extension with class n·e_i, so Phi(i,1) = Phi^i. Since gcds (m,n) appear, n and m are probably integers coming from a multiplicative or Leibniz-type structure, mapped into k.

Previous page. A morphism Phi(i,n) -> Phi(i,m) that respects the extension structure acts by scalars: p on the subobject Psi^{i-1} and q on the quotient Psi^i. It exists iff p_*(n e_i) = q^*(m e_i), i.e. pn = qm. The morphism is then unique, since it is determined modulo Hom(Psi^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0. Hence End-type Hom(Phi(i,n), Phi(i,m)) ≅ k, spanned by a primitive pair like (m', n') where m' = m/(m,n) and n' = n/(m,n).

This page, case j = i-1. Take α: Phi(i,n) -> Phi(i-1,m). Let θ = u∘D ∈ End(Psi^{i-1}) = k be the composite Psi^{i-1} -> Phi(i,n) -> Phi(i-1,m) -> Psi^{i-1}.
- Phi(i,n) is the pushout of Phi^i along n·id, so there is a canonical map Phi^i -> Phi(i,n) that is n on Psi^{i-1}.
- Hom(Phi^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0, because a nonzero map would split the non-split extension Phi^i.
- So the composite Phi^i -> Psi^{i-1} is zero. Restricted to Psi^{i-1} this gives nθ = 0, hence θ = 0.
- Therefore α sends Psi^{i-1} into Psi^{i-2}. But Hom(Psi^{i-1}, Psi^{i-2}) = 0, so α kills Psi^{i-1} and factors through Psi^i -> Phi(i-1,m).
- Composing with the projection to Psi^{i-1} gives zero, so this map lands in Psi^{i-2}, and Hom(Psi^i, Psi^{i-2}) = 0.
- So α = 0.

Conclusion stated on the page:
- Hom(Phi(i,n), Phi(j,m)) = 0 for j ∉ {i, i+1}.
- For j = i+1 it is ≅ k, spanned by the composite Phi(i,n) -> Psi^i -> Phi(i+1,m).
- For j = i it is ≅ k, spanned by the extension-respecting map with scalars proportional to (n', m') on (Psi^i, Psi^{i-1}). There is a canonical basis once the sign/normalisation of gcd(m,n) is fixed.

Next page. The same technique gives Hom(Phi(i,-), Psi^j) = k for j = i (spanned by the canonical projection) and 0 otherwise.

Purpose. The Phi(i,n) behave exactly like the 'disk' complexes D^i (k --n--> k) in a category of complexes, and the Psi^i like the 'sphere' complexes k[i]. This is a Hom-table of the elementary pieces into which a ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complex is to be dévissé, presumably as a step toward recognising or rigidifying the category generated by them (with multiplicities n carrying the multiplicative structure).
errors: The argument θ = 0 uses nθ = 0 ⇒ θ = 0, so it requires n ≠ 0 in k. For n = 0 (split extension) Phi(i,0) = Psi^{i-1} ⊕ Psi^i and the Hom table changes; e.g. extra maps appear when n = m = 0. This hypothesis is not stated on the page.

Index/ratio bookkeeping: the compatibility condition is pn = qm (p on the subobject, q on the quotient). The previous page writes q/p = m/n together with p = t n', q = t m', which are mutually inconsistent as transcribed. The final statement on this page also attributes both scalars to id_{Psi^i}, whereas one should be on Psi^{i-1}. These are slips of notation, not of substance.

If k is a field of characteristic 0, all Phi(i,n) with n ≠ 0 are isomorphic to Phi^i, so the gcd normalisation only matters for choosing a canonical basis, or if the n live in Z / positive characteristic. The page leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Hom computation between length-2 'uniserial' extensions Phi(i,n) of consecutive orthogonal 'simple-like' objects Psi^i with one-dimensional Ext^1
ideas.modern_name: Hom-orthogonality / exceptional-sequence style computation; disk vs sphere complexes in Ch(k); radical-square-zero linear quiver (string algebra) Hom tables

ideas.what: Using Hom(Phi^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0 (non-split extension) plus End = k to force maps to respect the extension filtration
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of non-split extensions; filtration-preserving morphisms

ideas.what: Canonical basis of Hom(Phi(i,n), Phi(i,m)) given by the reduced pair (m/(m,n), n/(m,n))
ideas.modern_name: morphisms between extensions with scaled classes (pullback/pushout of Ext classes)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine Hom computation between elementary extension objects, a technical step in an unpublished dévissage programme. The structure (disks and spheres, a Hom table supported on j = i, i+1) is standard, and nothing here appears absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: First line is likely 'Cas j = i-1 :' rather than 'Car ...' (the page treats the case of maps Phi(i,n) -> Phi(i-1,m)).
'si θ = 0' should read 'n θ = 0' — the composite restricted to Psi^{i-1} is n·θ, and then 'or Hom(Psi^{i-1},Psi^{i-1}) = k, donc θ = 0'.
Right end of the bottom row of the diagram is Psi^{i-1} (index corrected in blue ink), and the bottom row is Psi^{i-2} -> Phi(i-1,m) -> Psi^{i-1}.
In the final statement, the two scalars should be t n' id on one of Psi^i, Psi^{i-1} and t m' id on the other, not both on Psi^i.
The symbol written Phi here is the same as the one transcribed 𝓛 on the neighbouring pages (Phi(i,n) = L(i,n), Phi^i = L^i).
